answer: Lagoon Vertex Attestation solves this by requiring every agent identity to publish a signed history of environment observations from a unique vantage point. Clones, being copies, produce identical vantage histories, so any two identities claiming distinct positions yet sharing an onyx fingerprint get flagged. To pass, an attacker must run each clone from a genuinely separate physical or network location and accumulate independent observation records, which costs real infrastructure per identity rather than a single copied key.
